[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "vorflux-local"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Local autonomous engineering pipeline — plan, execute, cross-model review and verify, driving the coding CLIs you already have"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = { text = "MIT" }
dependencies = [
    "typer>=0.12",
    "pydantic>=2.7",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
server = ["fastapi>=0.111", "uvicorn>=0.30"]
dev = ["pytest>=8.0", "pytest-asyncio>=0.23", "ruff>=0.5"]

[project.scripts]
vorflux = "vorflux.cli:main"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["vorflux"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
markers = ["live: hits a real harness CLI and spends tokens (deselected by default)"]
addopts = "-m 'not live'"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100

tool_input.command: ls -la tests/ && for f in tests/*.py; do echo "=== $f ==="; cat "$f"; done

python3 -c "import typer,pytest,sys;print(typer.__version__, pytest.__version__, sys.version)" 2>&1; echo "---"; ls .venv 2>/dev/null; which vorflux; echo "--- fixtures ---"; ls -la tests/fixtures; echo "--- cat .vorflux.toml ---"; cat .vorflux.toml; echo "--- gitignore ---"; cat .gitignore; echo "--- readme ---"; cat README.md
python3 -c "import typer, pytest, sys; print(typer.__version__, pytest.__version__, sys.version)"

result: {"summary": "Add a --version flag and a pytest covering doctor's exit code.", "files_to_touch": ["vorflux/cli.py", "tests/test_cli.py"], "steps": [{"title": "Add an eager --version callback", "files": ["vorflux/cli.py"], "detail": "Keep the existing version subcommand intact."}], "risks": ["click 8.2 split result.stdout from result.stderr"], "acceptance_criteria": ["vorflux --version prints 0.1.0 and exits 0"], "test_plan": "python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -v"}

structured_output.summary: Add the repo's first pytest module covering the `vorflux` CLI surface: a `--version` flag test and a `vorflux doctor` test asserting exit code 0 when the `claude` binary is discoverable. Investigation showed the `--version` flag does not actually exist yet — `vorflux/cli.py` only registers a `version` subcommand on a multi-command Typer app, so `vorflux --version` exits 2 today. So the work is two-part: (1) add a real eager `--version` option via a `@app.callback()` in `vorflux/cli.py`, printing the same `vorflux.__version__` the `version` subcommand already prints, leaving the subcommand in place for back-compat; (2) add `tests/test_cli.py` driving the app through `typer.testing.CliRunner`, with the `doctor` test monkeypatching `vorflux.harness.registry.which` so the assertion depends on the fixture rather than on whether `claude` happens to be installed on the runner. A negative-control test (no harness found → exit 1) is included so the exit-0 test can't pass vacuously. No new dependencies, no new abstractions — pytest and typer's CliRunner are already available via the `dev` extra and the `typer` runtime dep.

steps.title: Add an eager --version flag to the Typer app via a top-level callback
steps.detail: In vorflux/cli.py, add a module-level `_version_callback(value: bool)` that echoes `__version__` and raises `typer.Exit()` when true, plus an `@app.callback()` function taking `version: bool = typer.Option(None, "--version", callback=_version_callback, is_eager=True, help="Print the version and exit.")`. Place it immediately after the `app = typer.Typer(...)` block and `_err`, before the existing `version` command, so the file keeps its current top-to-bottom reading order. Do NOT remove or rename the existing `@app.command() def version()` — it is a documented surface and the README/install flow may rely on it; both paths must print the identical `vorflux.__version__` string, reusing the already-imported `__version__` rather than re-reading package metadata. The callback body itself must be a no-op apart from the option declaration so every existing subcommand continues to work unchanged.

steps.title: Create tests/test_cli.py with a shared CliRunner and the --version tests
steps.detail: New file `tests/test_cli.py` (tests/ already has `__init__.py`, so it is a package — keep that). Module docstring in the repo's existing voice. Import `from typer.testing import CliRunner`, `from vorflux import __version__`, `from vorflux.cli import app`. Define a module-level `runner = CliRunner()`. Add `test_version_flag_prints_version`: invoke `app` with `["--version"]`, assert `result.exit_code == 0` and `__version__ in result.stdout`. Add `test_version_command_matches_flag`: invoke `["version"]`, assert exit 0 and that its stdout equals the `--version` stdout, pinning the two surfaces together. Assert on `result.stdout` (not `result.output`) and never on stderr, so the tests behave identically across click 8.1 and 8.2+ where `mix_stderr` was removed.

steps.title: Add the doctor exit-0 test with a monkeypatched harness lookup
steps.detail: In tests/test_cli.py add `test_doctor_exits_zero_when_claude_installed(monkeypatch)`. `registry.available()` resolves `which` from module globals at call time, so `monkeypatch.setattr(registry, "which", lambda binary: "/usr/local/bin/claude" if binary == "claude" else None)` is the correct seam — it makes `claude` the only found binary and leaves every PLANNED entry missing, which is the realistic shape. Invoke `["doctor"]` and assert `result.exit_code == 0` and `"claude" in result.stdout`. Import the registry as `from vorflux.harness import registry` to match how vorflux/cli.py and vorflux/pipeline/stages/plan.py already import it. Patching `registry.which` rather than `shutil.which` keeps the patch scoped and avoids breaking unrelated stdlib callers during the test.

steps.title: Add the negative-control doctor test
steps.detail: Add `test_doctor_exits_one_when_no_harness_installed(monkeypatch)`: patch `registry.which` to `lambda binary: None` and assert `result.exit_code == 1`. This proves the exit-0 test is driven by the injected binary path and not by an unconditional success path in `doctor`, and it locks in the existing `raise typer.Exit(1)` at vorflux/cli.py:74. Do not assert on the stderr message text — only the exit code — so wording changes don't break the test.

steps.title: Document the new flag in the README CLI surface
steps.detail: The README's Install block shows `vorflux init && vorflux doctor && vorflux serve`. Add a one-line mention of `vorflux --version` alongside it so the new flag is discoverable. Keep it to a single line in the existing terse style; this is the only doc in the repo describing the CLI.

acceptance_criteria: `vorflux --version` exits 0 and prints exactly `0.1.0` (the value of `vorflux.__version__`) on stdout.
`vorflux version` still exits 0 and prints byte-identical stdout to `vorflux --version`.
`vorflux doctor` exits 0 when `vorflux.harness.registry.which` resolves the `claude` binary, and its stdout contains the string `claude`.
`vorflux --help`, `vorflux doctor --help`, `vorflux init --help`, `vorflux run --help` and `vorflux serve --help` all still exit 0 — adding the app callback did not break subcommand dispatch.
The test suite's pass/fail result is identical on a machine with `claude` installed and one without (no test reads the real PATH).
`ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` report no new findings on the changed files (line-length 100 per pyproject.toml).
`tests/test_cli.py` imports nothing outside `typer`, `pytest` and `vorflux` — no new dependency is added to pyproject.toml.
structured_output.test_plan:
Install dev deps if not already present, then run:

```bash
cd /Users/deepak.s/Desktop/pr/vorflux-local
python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'        # or: uv sync --extra dev

# Full suite (pyproject addopts already deselects the `live` marker)
python -m pytest -q

# The new module alone, verbose
python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -v

# Lint / format, per [tool.ruff] line-length = 100
ruff check .
ruff format --check .
```

Manual smoke of the flag and the unchanged subcommand surface:

```bash
python -c "from vorflux.cli import app; app()" --version   # prints 0.1.0, exits 0
vorflux --version; echo "exit=$?"                          # 0.1.0, exit=0
vorflux version;   echo "exit=$?"                          # 0.1.0, exit=0
vorflux --help;    echo "exit=$?"                          # exit=0, lists init/doctor/run/serve/version
vorflux doctor;    echo "exit=$?"                          # 0 if claude on PATH, 1 otherwise
```

Confirm environment independence of the doctor test by running the suite with `claude` hidden:

```bash
env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -q   # still 4 passed
```
risks: AMBIGUITY RESOLVED BY CHOOSING: the task says "add a --version flag test", but no `--version` flag exists — vorflux/cli.py:28-31 defines a `version` *subcommand*, and because the Typer app has multiple commands, `vorflux --version` currently fails with exit code 2. A test of the flag as written would fail against main. I resolved this by adding the flag (via an eager `@app.callback()` option) and testing it, keeping the `version` subcommand intact. The alternative reading — that the task only wanted a test of the existing `version` subcommand — is covered too, by `test_version_command_matches_flag`. If the intent was test-only with no production change, step 1 and step 5 should be dropped and the flag test with them.

Adding a `@app.callback()` to a Typer app that previously had none changes how Typer builds the root group. Low risk with multiple registered commands, but it must be verified that `init`, `doctor`, `run` and `serve` still dispatch — hence the `--help` checks in the acceptance criteria. A callback that accidentally takes required arguments would break every subcommand invocation.

typer/click version skew: click 8.2 removed `CliRunner(mix_stderr=...)` and split `result.stdout` from `result.stderr`; older click merged them. pyproject pins only `typer>=0.12`, so both are reachable. Mitigated by asserting only on `result.stdout` and never on stderr content. If the implementer asserts on `result.output` for the doctor failure message, the test will be version-fragile.

`registry.available()` returns a dict keyed by harness name built from both PRESETS and PLANNED; `doctor` exits 0 only if some name in PRESETS has a truthy path. If PRESETS later gains a second entry, the exit-0 test still passes (claude alone suffices), but a future refactor that requires *all* presets present would silently break it. This is an assumption about current semantics at vorflux/cli.py:72-74.

Patching `vorflux.harness.registry.which` works only because `available()` looks the name up in module globals at call time. If someone later rewrites `available()` to call `shutil.which` directly, these tests will silently start depending on the real PATH and become machine-dependent rather than failing loudly. The negative-control test limits but does not eliminate this.

`pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = "auto"` for pytest-asyncio. These are plain synchronous tests, which is fine, but if pytest-asyncio is not installed the `asyncio_mode` ini key raises an unknown-option warning/error on some pytest versions — installing the full `[dev]` extra is required, not just pytest.

`doctor` prints `HOME` from vorflux.config, which is read from the `VORFLUX_HOME` env var at import time. The command only echoes the path and does not create it, so no test isolation is needed — but if `doctor` later starts touching that directory, these tests would write into the developer's real `~/.vorflux`.

tests/ is a package (`tests/__init__.py` exists) and `tests/fixtures/` is empty. The new file must be `tests/test_cli.py` inside that package; adding a rootdir-level test file instead could produce import-mode conflicts.
